rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly, so this candidate escalates obfuscation while retaining safety margins. SUB gets the strongest weights since instruction substitution carries near-zero runtime/size/correctness cost and is ideal for this tiny (1399-byte text) benchmark where every function benefits. BCF and IBR are pushed higher to add opaque predicates and indirect branching that frustrate static control-flow recovery, with moderate cost weights because the program is compute-light so some overhead is tolerable. FLA stays strong on security/diversity with a slightly raised CorrectnessRisk weight to be gentle with the C++ constructors (_ZN6sampleC1/C2Ev, _ZN3fsmC1/C2EP6triple) whose paired C1/C2 definitions make miscompilation observable. ICALL is favored moderately since main and fsm dispatch offer a few call sites to virtualize, but its CorrectnessRisk weight tempers aggressive indirecting around C++ linkage. SPLIT provides cheap synergy by enlarging basic-block pools for BCF/FLA to act on. IGV is kept as the weakest pass: with few globals in this benchmark its payoff is limited and its risk around C++ initialization order is the highest, so its elevated CorrectnessRisk weight lets the feature driver apply it only where global-access features clearly dominate.
